questions.stem: The machine that raises the anchor on most small vessels is the:
options: Windlass
Binnacle
Davit
Capstan
questions.explanation: A windlass handles anchor chain. A capstan has a vertical drum and is typically used for mooring lines.

questions.stem: Before maintenance on a crane or winch you should:
options: Work with the load suspended
Leave the hydraulics live to check for leaks
Run it at full load to test
Isolate and lock out the power and release stored energy
questions.explanation: Stored hydraulic and mechanical energy can move machinery unexpectedly.

questions.stem: A hydraulic winch reservoir is found much lower than normal. The best first response is:
options: Isolate the winch and look for a leak before topping up
Heat the oil
Top up and ignore the cause
Drain the tank
questions.explanation: Find and stop the leak to prevent damage and pollution.

questions.stem: A capstan differs from a winch because a capstan has:
options: A horizontal drum for storing wire
A vertical drum that the line wraps round and does not store it
No brake
A notched wheel for chain links
questions.explanation: A winch has a horizontal drum, usually storing wire or rope. A windlass has a gypsy for chain.

questions.stem: The clutch on a windlass or winch is used to:
options: Measure the load
Connect the drive to the drum or gypsy, or disconnect it so the anchor or line can run out
Cool the hydraulic oil
Tighten the wire rope
questions.explanation: With the clutch out, the brake alone controls the load.

questions.stem: Once the anchor is set and the vessel is lying to it, the strain should be held by the:
options: Windlass motor
Hydraulic pump
Capstan
Chain stopper or bow stopper, not the windlass
questions.explanation: The stopper takes the load so that the windlass and its brake are not overloaded.

questions.stem: The safest position when a mooring line or wire is under strain is:
options: Standing inside the bight of the line
Standing in line with the wire
Clear of the bight and out of line with the wire, in case it parts and recoils
Holding the line with a bare hand
questions.explanation: A parting line whips back along its length and snaps tight inside a bight.

questions.stem: A routine check of a deck winch wire rope should look for:
options: The colour of the strands
Broken strands, kinks, flattening and corrosion
How shiny it is
Whether it is longer than last year
questions.explanation: Broken strands, kinks and wear reduce strength, and a damaged wire must be replaced.

questions.stem: The maximum load stamped on a winch or crane is called the safe working load. You should:
options: Treat it as a target to reach
Allow loads up to double it in calm weather
Never exceed it, and allow for shock loads in a seaway
Ignore it for the first lift of the day
questions.explanation: The SWL includes a safety margin, and wave motion adds shock load.
